newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram tells RBI to cut lending rates.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram tells RBI to cut lending rates.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told India's central bank on Monday that interest rates should be reduced to support economic growth.

Chidambaram told Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan that the annual inflation rate should be kept at six to seven percent to provide economic and political stability, the RBI said in a statement released in the capital.

"Finance Minister also urged that while there has been some softening of interest rates since October 1996, it is not enough and further reduction of lending rates would be desirable and possible," the RBI statement said.

It quoted Chidambaram as telling the RBI governor that price stability is critical since it is a key to maintaining growth and "inflation should be contained at 6-7 percent as this would provide both economic and poltical stability".
The finance minister also urged the central bank chief to encourage bankers to lend more actively as credit had expanded slowly.

The RBI governor acknowledged that the flow of credit had remained low. "Measures necessary to accelerate the flow of credit to support growth in output will merit attention," the statement quoted Rangarajan as saying.
